001: Did you get the email with the instructions for the monthly report?
Yes, I read it this morning. Do you want to go over it together?
That would be really helpful, because there are a couple of points I'm not clear on.
Sure, tell me which ones and we'll look at them right now.
Especially the expenses part, I don't know if we have to itemize each invoice.
Oh, yes, you have to attach all the invoices, but without breaking down the taxes.
002: Excuse me, could you give me more details on how you want the summary?
Sure, I prefer you start with the conclusions and then put the data.
Understood, and do you want me to include the figures from the previous quarter?
Yes, but only as a reference, in a brief comparison table.
Perfect, then I'll structure it in three sections: conclusions, data, and comparison.
Exactly, and remember to turn it in to me before Friday at noon.
003: I've finished the draft of the sales report, do you mind taking a look at it?
Of course not, give it to me and I'll look at it right now.
Thanks, I'm mainly worried about whether the objectives section is well written.
At first glance it's fine, but I think you should be more specific with the dates.
You're right, I'll add the deadline for each phase of the project.
Good idea, that way the report will be much clearer and more professional.
004: How do you prefer I present the results to you, in a meeting or in writing?
I prefer you send it to me in writing first, and then we'll discuss it in person.
Okay, is it fine if I send it to you this afternoon?
Yes, perfect, that way I have time to read it calmly before the meeting.
Alright, then I'll send it to you as soon as I finish reviewing the latest data.
Great, and if you have any questions while writing it, don't hesitate to ask me.
005: I don't really understand this instruction about recording overtime hours.
Let's see, let me look at it. Oh, yes, it means you have to enter them in the system before the end of the month.
And is it done individually or does the head of each team do it?
Normally each employee does it, but the supervisor has to approve it afterwards.
I see, so I have to ask my supervisor for approval.
Exactly, and if you have any problems with the system, let me know and I'll help you.
006: I received the instructions for the new project, but they seem a bit confusing to me.
What part did you get lost on? Maybe I can explain it to you in a different way.
Mainly the task distribution, I don't know who's in charge of each part.
Look, in the document there's a chart with the people responsible for each area.
Oh, that's right, I hadn't seen it. Then I have a clearer picture now.
I'm glad, and if you have another question, I'm here for whatever you need.
007: Is it okay if I include the charts in the final report?
Yes, I think it's a good idea, but make sure they're well explained.
Of course, I'll put a brief description under each chart.
Perfect, and don't forget to cite the source of the data in each one.
Good point, I'll keep that in mind. Anything else I should review?
Just the conclusion, that it's concise and summarizes the main points well.
008: Have you had time to review the report I sent you yesterday?
Yes, I read the whole thing and overall I thought it was very thorough.
I'm glad to hear that, but is there anything you would change?
Just one detail: in the introduction, I think it's missing a mention of the market context.
You're right, I'll add a brief paragraph about the current situation in the sector.
Great, with that change the report will be complete.
009: For the activity report, do we also have to include the day-to-day tasks?
No, only the main tasks and the projects you've participated in.
Understood, then I'll focus on the projects and leave out the routine tasks.
That's right, and don't forget to indicate the time spent on each project.
Okay, I'll write it all down with the estimated hours for each one.
Very good, that way the report will be much more useful for the evaluation.
010: Could you explain to me how the new system for submitting reports works?
Sure, it's very simple: you log into the platform, create a new report, and follow the template.
And does the template already come with the predefined sections?
Yes, you just have to fill in each section and attach the necessary documents.
Perfect, it seems pretty easy to use.
It is, and if you have any questions, there's a manual with examples on the intranet.
